{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks-per-node=1
#   --cpus-per-task=1
#   --gres=gpu:1
#   --mem=40GB
#   --time=12:00:00
#   --job-name=2Lsim

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=12h
#flux: --job-name=2Lsim

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=40GB
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

module purge

# Slurm variable $SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK is not set under Flux.
# Use the allocated cores-per-task (here: 1).
export NUM_JULIA_THREADS=$(nproc)

# Slurm variable $SLURM_JOB_ID is not set under Flux.
# Use Flux job id if available; fall back to shell PID.
JOBID=${FLUX_JOB_ID:-$$}

rundir=$SCRATCH/twolayer_simulation/$JOBID
mkdir -p "$rundir"
cp TwoLayerSimulation.jl Driver.jl driver.sbatch "$rundir" 2>/dev/null || true
cp Parameters.jl "$rundir"/Parameters.jl
cd "$rundir"

# Match Slurm invocation: julia -t $SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK (1)
julia -t 1 Driver.jl > run.log
"
}

reasons: The original Slurm job required a GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.
The original Slurm job requested 40GB memory (`--mem=40GB`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this may under-provision the job and risk OOM.
issues: Resource-related: `export NUM_JULIA_THREADS=$(nproc)` may exceed the allocated cores (`#flux: -c 1`), potentially oversubscribing the node if Julia uses that variable.
